newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU may publish new wheat tender rule next week.
newsitem.headline: EU may publish new wheat tender rule next week.

text.p: A new regulation is likely to be published next week that will prevent traders from submitting bids to export free-market soft wheat with a tax through the weekly EU tender channel, the Coceral EU grain trade association said on Friday.
The EU grain panel on Thursday voted the change to EU regulation 1147/96, scrapping tax tenders for wheat, it said.
Since last December traders have been able to submit bids to export EU soft wheat with taxes and/or subsidies at the weekly tenders. The Commission could grant exports with taxes and/or refunds.
But until now it has resisted pressure to restore subsidies, with the exception of a special tender to African, Caribbean and Pacific nations.
EU officials have said the Commission was unlikely to restore wheat subsidies as long as some traders were willing to pay a tax.
If the new regulation is published in the EU official journal before next Thursday, it would apply to the next round of EU weekly grain tenders, trade sources said.
